mechanism_narrative: The sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past two weeks indicates a growing public willingness to engage in out-of-home activities, which will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility signals a broader return to commuting and general movement, directly translating into increased footfall for retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing GROCERY_PHARM visits suggests people are spending less time at home and making more frequent trips, indicating a behavioral shift that will boost incidental retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease while GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained increase in WORKPLACES mobility over the past three weeks, despite a slight recent dip, reflects an ongoing policy-driven return to offices, which will continue to provide a baseline uplift for retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility reverses its upward trend, and RETAIL_REC also declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A recent week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility suggests a shift towards outdoor leisure activities, which will divert footfall away from indoor retail and recreation, leading to a slight decline in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 3 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC also increases in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained shift away from home-based activities, freeing up time and inclination for out-of-home retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous week-on-week increase in both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT mobility indicates a broad resurgence in daily routines involving multiple stops and increased movement, which will spill over into and boost retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: Both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT increase week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC declines in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent stagnation in WORKPLACES mobility after a strong prior rise suggests a temporary plateau in the return-to-office trend, which could temporarily dampen further RETAIL_REC growth over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility shows less than 1 point week-on-week change after a period of >5 point weekly increases
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility stagnates or slightly declines, but RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the following week.
